summary: Ten criminal cases were filed at the Fairbanks courthouse on Nov. 2. Seven are charges of theft of property worth less than $250, with offense dates between Sep. 21 and Oct. 30, and in five of those a summons was issued rather than an arrest made, with none recording an arrest. One of the ten is a domestic violence assault charge against Angel Eva Michelle Aishanna, arising from an arrest by Alaska State Troopers on Nov. 1 that an earlier edition reported as having no court case; she was arraigned the same day the case was filed. The other new cases are a charge of theft of property worth $250 to $749 and a charge of possessing a small amount of a controlled substance. The court's weekly criminal filings report covers Oct. 26 to Nov. 1 and so does not include any of the Nov. 2 filings; its counts are 36 cases at Fairbanks, four at Nenana, two at Delta Junction and none at Healy. Earlier on Nov. 2 the court's weekly dispositions report recorded the dismissal of a first-degree murder charge against Brian Jeffery Davenport on a finding that he is not competent to stand trial, two assault convictions for Kyle Douglas Folger, and the closure of nine case numbers on which no charge was ever filed. Alaska State Troopers reported no incidents in the Fairbanks area for Nov. 2 and Fairbanks Police reported no arrests. No case was filed at the Nenana, Healy or Delta Junction courthouses.

entries.title: Domestic violence assault charge: Angel Eva Michelle Aishanna
body: Angel Eva Michelle Aishanna, 34, of Fairbanks, is charged with assault in the fourth degree — recklessly causing physical injury to another person — a Class A misdemeanor. The court file records the count as domestic violence related.

A residence in Fairbanks, Nov. 1 at 2:19 p.m.; Alaska State Troopers. Troopers say they responded to a report of a domestic disturbance, that their investigation determined she assaulted a household member, and that she was taken into custody without incident and taken to the Fairbanks Correctional Center.

Case 4FA-26-02214CR, filed Nov. 2. She was arraigned the same day, a public defender was appointed and release conditions were set. The next court date is Dec. 10. She is arrested and charged, not convicted.
The troopers' dispatch gives her name as Aishanna Angel; the court record gives it as Aishanna, Angel Eva Michelle. The age is as the troopers' dispatch states it.

entries.title: Murder charge dismissed: Brian Jeffery Davenport
body: The charge of murder in the first degree against Brian Jeffery Davenport, 29, of Fairbanks, was dismissed on Oct. 8. The charge was intent to cause death, an unclassified felony, and it was the only count on the file.

The court record gives the reason for the dismissal as a finding that the defendant is not competent to stand trial. The dismissal followed a contested competency hearing on Oct. 5, according to KTVF, which reports that he had been held at the Alaska Psychiatric Institute in Anchorage and that prosecutors had asked for a further period in which to restore him to competency.
The offense was recorded at Fairbanks on Jan. 20, 2026 and the case was filed Jan. 21. Police said he admitted taking a handgun and shooting a woman at a Fairbanks home, according to KTVF.
Case 4FA-26-00112CR. No future hearing is set and the case database records the case as closed. A dismissal is not a conviction and not an acquittal.

entries.title: Assault convictions: Kyle Douglas Folger
body: Kyle Douglas Folger was convicted on Oct. 12 of assault in the fourth degree — recklessly causing physical injury to another person — and of assault when a child is present. Both are Class A misdemeanors, and both convictions followed guilty pleas.
A third count, assault in the third degree by causing injury with a weapon, a Class C felony, was dismissed by the prosecution.
All three counts were recorded at Fairbanks with an offense date of Apr. 20, 2026. Case 4FA-26-00703CR.
No sentence is stated in the court's dispositions report. No future hearing is set on the case number.

entries.title: Domestic violence assault charges: Ernest A Keith
body: Ernest A Keith is charged with assault in the fourth degree — recklessly causing physical injury to another person — and with three counts of assault when a child is present, which is committing an assault while a child is present. All four counts are Class A misdemeanors, and the court file records three of the four as domestic violence related.
The offense is recorded at Fairbanks on Nov. 1 and the charges were filed the same day.
Case 4FA-26-02209CR. A pre-trial conference is set for Dec. 24 and a trial week for Jan. 4, 2027. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: DUI and fugitive from justice charges: Chad James De Long
body: Chad James De Long is charged with driving under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance — operating a vehicle while impaired — with refusal to submit to a chemical test, and with driving while his license was canceled, revoked or suspended for a criminal offense. All three are Class A misdemeanors.
The offense is recorded at Delta Junction on Oct. 31. Case 4FA-26-02210CR, filed at the Fairbanks courthouse on Nov. 1; a pre-trial conference is set for Dec. 24 and a trial week for Jan. 4, 2027.

A second file, case 4FA-26-02211CR, charges him as a fugitive from justice under the provision for arrest before a requisition — a holding charge used while another state's demand for a person is awaited. Arraignment on that file is set for Nov. 3 and a fugitive from justice hearing for Dec. 1.
He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Charges dismissed for want of probable cause: Jess Lee Antonich Eakin
body: Two charges against Jess Lee Antonich Eakin were dismissed on Oct. 26 for want of probable cause. They were unlawful contact in violation of a court order — contacting a person the court had ordered him not to contact — and violating conditions of release in a misdemeanor case.
Both counts were recorded at Fairbanks with an offense date of Oct. 22. Case 4FA-26-02165CR.
No conviction was entered. The case number is no longer served by the state's public case database, and the dismissal is recorded in the court's weekly dispositions report.

entries.title: Nine court case numbers that the state case database no longer serves are recorded as closed with no charge ever filed
body: Nine criminal case numbers that the Alaska Court System's online case database returns no records for are listed in the court's weekly dispositions report as closed cases. Each carries a single count recorded as a charging document pending or not filed, which means no charge was ever filed against the person on that file.

Four were closed on Oct. 31: 4FA-26-02197CR, 4FA-26-02202CR and 4FA-26-02206CR at Fairbanks, and 4DJ-26-00067CR at Delta Junction. One, 4FA-26-02124CR, was closed Oct. 23. The remaining four were closed earlier in October: 4FA-26-01984CR on Oct. 1, 4FA-26-02004CR and 4FA-26-02013CR on Oct. 3, and 4FA-26-02008CR on Oct. 5.

A case number is issued when a person is booked, before the district attorney decides whether to file a charge. Where no charge is filed the case is closed, and the public database then stops serving the number.
Readers looking up any of these numbers in the public case database will find nothing. The dispositions report is the record that states what became of them.
